title: GRADE Summary of Findings: certainty of the evidence for perioperative biologic continuation in patients with psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis undergoing orthopaedic surgery.
rows: Infection or wound complications, continue versus hold (OR)
4 (1,979 analysis units: procedures in 3 studies, patients in 1)

Downgraded for risk of bias (unadjusted and era-based designs, unblinded SSI adjudication), inconsistency (directional heterogeneity, high I2), indirectness (PsA not isolated, heterogeneous SSI definitions, mixed surgery), and imprecision (sparse events, wide CI). Confounding by indication most likely flatters continuation, because sicker patients and higher-risk operations were preferentially selected for a hold.

Downgraded for risk of bias (univariate and underpowered Borgas and Nguyen analyses, unvalidated PJI code), indirectness (PsA not isolated, recent-infliximab proxy), and imprecision (very sparse; the pool is dominated by George).
Single registry cohort; unmatched and imbalanced comparison plus immortal-time selection; objective revision endpoint. Narrative and synthesis-without-meta-analysis only.
caption: Certainty was rated Very low for every outcome. Participant counts are analysis units, because the contributing studies counted procedures, surgeries, or patients and those units are not interchangeable; each cell states the composition. This is a summary of certainty, not an extraction table: study-level event data are given in Table S3, the primary forest plot is Figure 2, and sensitivity and robustness analyses are given in Table S4. The primary comparative estimate is model-dependent, since fixed-effect, Mantel-Haenszel, and Peto models all return about 0.97, and every estimate crosses an odds ratio of 1.
abbreviations: Abbreviations: CI, confidence interval; GRADE, Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation; I2, percentage of variability across studies attributable to heterogeneity rather than chance; k, number of studies; OR, odds ratio; PJI, periprosthetic joint infection; PsA, psoriatic arthritis; SSI, surgical-site infection; THA, total hip arthroplasty; TNFi, tumor necrosis factor inhibitor.
